summary: Typosquat package exfiltrates host identifiers to webhook.site on install
details: Package name impersonates the legitimate `use-sync-external-store` React shim while its `package.json` description ('A utility for managing SVG buckets') is unrelated to that purpose. `package.json` declares a `postinstall` hook running `node index.js`, which reads `os.hostname()` and `process.cwd()` and POSTs them as JSON to a hardcoded webhook at `https://webhook.site/0a4d6535-e2dd-46b7-aff7-8af65c145c50`. The exfiltration fires automatically during `npm install` without any user interaction and sends installer host identifiers to an attacker-controlled collector. The shape — misleading name, mismatched description, install-time beacon to an anonymous webhook endpoint — is the recon/confirmation stage of a typosquat supply-chain attack.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
